items_missed: Opened by apologizing twice, including a technical excuse - 'sorry for the. Well one, my headphones not working just a moment ago but also not reaching back out to you yesterday.' The first thing the customer heard was a problem, not a plan
No agenda statement of any kind - no roadmap, no timeframe, no 'sound good?'
Never asked 'how are you today?'

Never asked for the booking, on a call where the customer was clearly ready. She asked 'Are you all available on the fourteenth?', he confirmed the date was open, and she then asked 'When do I need to finalize my decision?' - two buying signals in a row - and his answer was 'it doesn't expire or anything like that.' He removed every reason to decide and closed with 'just let us know when you make a decision'

Never mentioned no deposit. She literally asked when she has to commit; 'there's no deposit, so booking it costs you nothing and holds the crew' was the answer to the question she asked, and it never came
No email handoff - he pointed her back at Eric's existing 8/21 email instead of saying a fresh confirmation or quote email was coming from him
No bolded key-details list explained, and no 'reply with any corrections' to get the move details verified
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' and no business hours given

Contradicted the written estimate mid-sentence and never resolved it - 'the estimate itself previously was that same team of five movers for somewhere in the six to seven hour range. Generally a 2700 square foot home it's usually gonna take somewhere in the better part of an eight to nine hour day.' At $510/hr that is a $1,020 spread. The customer then anchored on the low number ('if it's five to an hour and 6:00 to seven hours...') and he did not correct her. This is our estimate-accuracy problem happening live

Let the customer teach him the clock rules. She read the 2.5 hour minimum and the 15-minute increments off her own notes and he answered 'Yeah. Right. Yes.' He never stated that the clock starts on site when the contract opens, and never sense-checked it
Never stated the per-mover-per-hour structure in his own words - only the $510 team total, and only after she recited it first

No No Worries Damage Coverage. Worse than silence: he listed 'insurance' as included in the hourly rate without ever explaining the $2,000 coverage or the 60 cents/lb baseline - on a call where he spent his longest turn worrying out loud about damaging her leather couches
No Meet Your Mover email pitch
No On-Time Guarantee, despite handing her a live arrival window - '8:30 AM to 9:00 AM arrival time' was the perfect setup and nothing followed it
No 'pricing is super simple' opener
Packing never raised - never asked whether they need packing services and never priced them, on a 2700 sqft move two and a half weeks out
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped. Low box count and 17 days of runway is the ideal window for it - no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip
No stairs, walk distance, parking, access, additional-stops or storage-stops confirmation, and none of these explained as variables that move the number

No moving-stressor question. She said 'we have had way too much experience moving' - a customer telling you she has been burned before - and got 'Yeah.' No exploration, no reassurance, no differentiation off it

Chronic hedging undercut his own expertise - five 'I don't think's in a single turn ('I don't think that the original estimate was too far off... I don't think it's certainly we don't need more than that... I don't think we're gonna come in. Well below that')
Used the customer's name once, in the greeting, and never again
top_strength: He did the homework and it showed. He actually watched the virtual walkthrough video before dialing, validated the 5-mover/2-truck resourcing against what he saw, and gave a real reason for the second truck that was about protecting her property rather than padding the bill - 'we have extra space for some of your other, you know, the leather couches we don't wanna, we'll wrap them up, we don't want to stack on top of them.' His answer to 'are those the total fees' was also the strongest block on the call and near-perfect against the rubric: truck, taxes, insurance, blankets, stretch wrap, bands and tools all included, then 'no fees for booking or cancellation credit card processing fees, mileage heavy items items going upstairs, no fees of any type.' And he caught a real service gap on his own initiative - the only email on file was Neil's, so he added her Yahoo address and explained that anyone at Einstein can now pull the profile up.
coaching_note: Khevan, you earned the close on this call and then did not ask for it. She asked if the 14th was open, you said yes, and then she asked how long she has to decide - that is a customer asking you to close her. The exact words: 'Great news, the 14th is still open. There's no deposit, so let's lock that crew in for you right now - nothing is committed financially, and if anything changes we just move it.' Nothing else on this call is worth as many points as that one sequence. Second priority, and it is the one Amanda will care about: you gave her two different estimates in the same breath - 'six to seven hour range' from Eric's written quote, then 'the better part of an eight to nine hour day' for a 2700 sqft home - and she walked away repeating the lower one back to you unchallenged. If the written estimate is light, say so and reset it on the call: 'I want to be straight with you - the estimate on file says 6 to 7 hours, but for a 2700 square foot home I'd plan on 8, and here's what would bring it down.' That is the whole estimate-accuracy fix in one sentence, and it protects you on move day. Third: you also gave away the No Worries pitch. You spent your longest turn on the call telling her how carefully you'd handle her leather couches - that is the natural on-ramp to 'and we back that with up to $2,000 in No Worries Damage Coverage, included.' Last, a delivery note: drop the headphones apology from the open and cut the 'I don't think' hedging. She has moved many times and is reading her own notes back to you; she needs you to sound like the expert in the room, which you are. One more piece of context for whoever coaches this: this was a follow-up on an already-completed virtual walkthrough, so the light Probe score partly reflects information legitimately captured in the video, not a discovery failure - the booking ask, the estimate contradiction, the clock and the differentiators are the real gaps.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and cooperative with a few genuine affirmations ('Yeah, of course', 'Perfect, I've got you added in there') and one real moment of care about her leather couches, but he was passive for most of the call - monosyllabic 'Yeah. Right. Yes.' while the customer explained the pricing structure to him, an apologetic open, heavy hedging, no humor, and her 'we have had way too much experience moving' rapport hook left on the floor.
audio_review_reason: Short call (5.6 min, 37 lines) in which the customer carried much of the explanatory load, so transcript signal is thin - the clipped 'Yeah/Right/Yes' acknowledgments and heavy hedging could be genuinely flat delivery or could read as warm and attentive on audio. Worth a listen before coaching him on tone, especially since he is a Branch Manager.
